summary: Implemented a scoped, observation-only Codex Mission port composing existing dispatch, executor, effect guard and invocation journal interfaces. The post-repair functional suite executed 58 tests with 58 PASS, zero failures and exit 0. Native M2 E2E and acceptance remain unproven.
functional_delta: C4 context: the stock Mission DAG remains the sole controller. Native admission supplies authenticated READY/credential verifiers, current source digest and effect snapshots; independent QA and the coordinator retain terminal authority. No competing task store, runner, scheduler, lease administration or CLI was added.

C4 component boundary: CodexMissionPort.dispatch(CodexPortRequest): Promise<CodexPortObservation> composes CodexDispatchBinding.dispatch, its existing Pick<CodexExecutor, run>, preflightEffect/authorizeEffect and Pick<ExecutionInvocationJournal, prepare | markDispatched>. codexPortInputDigest(CodexDispatchRequest): string binds prompt, invocation, principal/session, authorization reference, plan digest, epoch and timeout without hashing credentials into an exposed request body.

Ownership: new implementation, focused Node test and this result artifact are the only three changed files. Existing executor, binding, guard, journal, Mission index and BMad source of truth are read-only and preserved. Direct module import is the compatible interface; no barrel export was modified.

Bind journal intent to invocation, source SHA256, input SHA256, policy SHA256, owner/session, decision reference, generation and plan revision. Snapshot and freeze request data before asynchronous verification to prevent caller mutation during dispatch.

Reuse the stock journal's atomic markDispatched dispatchRef winner semantics with a fresh unique reference: only the persisted winner may invoke the binding. Dispatched or completed receipts require reconciliation, never automatic replay. Prepared-only recovery may proceed once. The port deliberately never calls recordOutcome or settles a Mission.

Recheck live authenticated effect authorization and source identity immediately before the stock executor call; retain stock credential, invocation, lease and epoch checks. Recheck lease, epoch, effect and source after an otherwise observed result. Authority loss, ambiguous timeout, adapter/provenance failure or persistence uncertainty fail closed without terminal GREEN.

Require a positive integer PID, exactly one matching stock thread.started event, matching mission/task/invocation/thread/PID/source in dispatch.receipt, exit zero and the independent trusted physical provenance verifier before treating process completion as observed. Exit zero or turn.completed alone cannot become accepted evidence.

Systematic debugging RED/GREEN: a new prototype-based verifier regression reproduced 57 PASS / 1 FAIL / exit 1 because object spreading dropped prototype methods. Explicit forwarding preserves both methods and receiver binding; fresh retest produced 58 PASS / 0 FAIL / exit 0.

Focused coverage includes actual stock CodexExecutor code with an injected fake spawn, credential/invocation denial, stale lease/epoch, source and input mismatch, scope/revision/fence revocation across awaits, missing or conflicting thread/PID/receipt evidence, untrusted provenance, timeout/replay, crash-state recovery, concurrent port instances, journal failures, caller mutation and verifier compatibility. Fixture outcomes are not Native E2E authority.

BMad gate: v3/docs/validation/m2-r7-bmad-scope.md establishes bounded M2 implementation and UNACCEPTED pending independent QA; ADR-406 is Proposed. BMad Help, Quick Dev steps and templates, systematic-debugging, adversarial-general and verification-before-completion were loaded. Scope-specific instructions override unavailable skill scripts, new spec files, interactive checkpoints and subagent requirements; no independent review is claimed.

Wire the direct-module port into a stock Native admission caller only under separate write authority. The read-only Mission index and existing runtime callers were not changed.

Trusted host must supply real authenticated READY/credential verification, canonical live effect snapshots, lease/epoch readback, source digest readback and independent physical receipt provenance. Callback fixtures and an authenticated boolean alone are not deployment authority.

Actual Codex CLI and a cryptographically or physically trusted dispatch.receipt producer were not launched. The stock executor adapter was exercised with a fake process; stock CLI output is not assumed to supply the custom receipt automatically.

Journal concurrency/restart cases exercise a contract-compatible in-memory adapter. The actual durable journal's file locking and storage/restart integration were source-reviewed but not executed because its dependency tree and runtime writes are outside this task scope.

The port intentionally leaves every dispatched attempt pending reconciliation/independent QA, including known process failure and pre-spawn denial after reservation. It never upgrades journal status or auto-retries an ambiguous invocation.

Full package typecheck/build/lint, public export integration, live process/PID provenance, installed-package compatibility and cross-process durability remain unverified. Node type stripping does not constitute a TypeScript build.

Only scoped source evidence was available: no live graph index, full AGENTS hierarchy discovery, git dirty-state inspection or independent skill-review agent was run. No whole-worktree cleanliness or Native E2E claim is made.
